nodes.label: System Collector
nodes.description: Gathers comprehensive system information: CPU (model, cores, freq, load), memory (total, used, swap), disk (mounts, usage, I/O, SMART), network (interfaces, IPs, RX/TX), kernel (version, modules), hardware (sensors, USB, PCI), processes (top consumers, zombie count), and OS details (version, packages, updates). Reads /proc, /sys, uses gopsutil, and shells out to sensors/lsblk/lspci for hardware data.

nodes.label: Journal Reader
nodes.description: Reads and analyzes systemd journal logs via sd-journal or journalctl. Filters by priority (error/warning/info), detects boot-time failures, slow services, service crashes, and recurring error patterns. Maintains a rolling buffer of recent entries with pattern matching for known Ubuntu error signatures.

nodes.label: Service Checker
nodes.description: Verifies systemd service health: lists all services with status (active/failed/enabled/disabled), checks user services, detects flapping services (high restart counts), and validates expected states. Parses systemctl JSON output and maintains service profiles with expected states for deviation detection.

nodes.label: Health Check Engine
nodes.description: Runs 8 categories of diagnostic checks against configurable thresholds: CPU (high load, thermal throttling), memory (low free, swap thrashing, OOM risk), disk (space >90%, SMART warnings, high I/O wait), network (interface down, packet loss), kernel (panics, OOM activity), service (failures, flapping), system (time sync, AppArmor, filesystem), and boot (slow boot, failed targets). Returns pass/warn/fail/critical with overall 0-100 health score.

nodes.label: Config Manager
nodes.description: Manages YAML configuration at ~/.config/sysdiag/config.yaml with threshold overrides, enabled checks, monitoring interval, alert preferences, export settings, database retention, and baseline learning mode. Supports env var overrides (SYSDIAG_*) and CLI flags (highest priority). Validates config on load with sensible defaults and hot-reload via SIGHUP.

nodes.label: Continuous Monitor
nodes.description: Daemon mode with periodic health checks (default: 5 min intervals). Detects state changes (delta detection), runs anomaly detection against learned baselines, and reports auto-recovery events. Implements resource-aware scheduling that skips heavy collection when system is busy. Runs as a systemd user service with graceful degradation.

nodes.label: Diagnostic Database
nodes.description: SQLite database (pure Go via modernc.org/sqlite) with tables for snapshots (timestamped full system state), checks_history (trending data), thresholds (custom overrides), baselines (learned normal ranges), alerts (deduplication), and config (key-value store). Uses WAL mode for concurrent reads during monitoring, auto-prunes snapshots older than 30 days, maintains rolling window of last 1000 checks per type.

nodes.label: Report Builder
nodes.description: Generates reports in multiple formats: terminal (color-coded, health score, sectioned details), JSON (machine-parseable for tooling), HTML (single-file with collapsible sections and inline charts), Markdown (for docs/issues/wikis), and plaintext (for piping). Template-based rendering using Go text/template and html/template with embedded templates.

nodes.label: Alert Engine
nodes.description: Delivers desktop notifications via D-Bus/libnotify for critical findings. Supports immediate notifications for critical issues, batched digests (every 15 min) for warnings, and recovery notifications with alert references. Deduplicates identical alerts within 1-hour window and rate-limits to max 10/hour. Falls back to notify-send exec if D-Bus library unavailable.

nodes.label: Export Handler
nodes.description: Writes diagnostic results to files at ~/sysdiag/exports/<timestamp>-<format>.ext with atomic temp+rename writes and proper permissions (600 config, 644 exports). Supports piping to stdout for chaining (sysdiag report --format json | jq). Can archive multiple snapshots as tar.gz bundles. Auto-creates directories on first export.

nodes.label: CLI Commander
nodes.description: Main entry point powered by cobra CLI with subcommands: sysdiag (quick summary), scan (full diagnostic), monitor (daemon mode), report (generate report), status (health overview), history (trend data), alerts (manage), config (view/edit), export (save to file), baselines (manage), version, help. Interactive TUI mode using bubbletea library with real-time dashboard, tabbed sections (CPU/Memory/Disk/Network/Services/Logs), color-coded health indicators, and keyboard navigation.
